q: Which products are profitable after returns and advertising costs?

answer:
Yes — in the last 30 days these products show positive product-level net profit after returns and allocated ad spend (product P&L net profit (allocated), product-level P&L with allocated ad spend). Top profitable products (last 30 days, order-date P&L, default brand Tilting Heads):

- Pawveralls Pro Suspender Boots — ₹34,113 (net profit)  
- LaserPlay Collar — ₹5,549  
- DuckDash Treat Toy — ₹5,487  
- Play Scratch Lounge — ₹4,556

What this means
- These product figures are true net profit after returns and allocated ad spend (product P&L net profit (allocated) = net sales − net COGS − allocated ad spend). The numbers are positive, so these SKUs contributed to P&L profit in the period.
- Magnitude matters: Pawveralls Pro Suspender Boots is far ahead of the rest (₹34k vs next-high ₹5.5k), so it’s the largest single product contributor.
- This result is scoped to the default brand (Tilting Heads) and uses product-level P&L (allocated ad spend); other brands or an order-date vs event-date P&L view would differ.

Worth checking: drill the product P&L net profit (allocated) down by product to see ad spend and return components (product P&L ad spend (allocated) and product return revenue (P&L basis)) for the top products.
